statusNote: As of November 21, 2026, Congress has not passed a new funding law since the stopgap signed September 2. Both deadlines still stand.

cliffs.label: December 11
cliffs.headline: The stopgap runs out
cliffs.summary: The stopgap law that keeps the government open ends on December 11. Many program extensions it carried end the same day.
cliffs.law: P.L. 119-103 (H.R. 6500), the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027, signed September 2, 2026

cliffs.label: December 31
cliffs.headline: Year-end health and family programs
cliffs.summary: A second batch of health and safety net programs runs out at the end of the year. These dates were set by earlier laws, not by the stopgap.
cliffs.law: P.L. 119-75, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, and earlier health laws

items.title: Government funding
items.whatStops: Agencies without a full-year budget must stop work that is not essential. That is a shutdown.
items.whoFeelsIt: Federal workers and contractors, and anyone waiting on a federal office for a permit, loan, or answer.
items.mechanics: Section 106(3) of Division A ends stopgap funding on December 11, 2026, unless a full-year funding law passes first. Funding lapses at 12:01 a.m. Eastern on December 12.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Overview of Continuing Appropriations for FY2027
Senate-passed bill text, H.R. 6500 (govinfo)

items.title: Flood insurance (NFIP)
items.whatStops: FEMA can no longer sell new flood insurance policies. Home sales in flood zones that need a policy can stall.
items.whoFeelsIt: People buying or refinancing a home in a mapped flood zone. Policies already in force keep paying claims until their one-year term ends.

reach.label: flood insurance policies, with about $1.3 trillion in coverage

items.extra: In the June 2010 lapse, estimates suggest over 1,400 home sale closings were canceled or delayed each day. That is a past estimate, not a 2026 forecast.
items.mechanics: Section 139 extends both the authority to write new flood policies and the program's $30.425 billion Treasury borrowing limit through the stopgap. On a lapse, borrowing authority falls to $1 billion (42 U.S.C. 4016(a), 4026).

sources.label: CRS IN10835, NFIP reauthorization and lapse
CRS R49353, Section 139

items.title: Highway, transit and rail programs
items.whatStops: The law that lets the Transportation Department run highway, transit, rail and road safety programs runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: State road and transit agencies that count on federal money, and the crews and contractors they pay.
items.mechanics: Division C, the Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2026, sets an extension end date of December 11, 2026 (Sec. 3002, 3101). Highway Trust Fund spending authority moves to December 12, 2026 (Sec. 3201).

sources.label: Senate text of the extension divisions (Aug 2, 2026)
White House signing notice

items.title: E-Verify
items.whatStops: The legal authority for E-Verify, the online check employers use to see if a new hire can work in the U.S., runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: Employers who use it, including those required to by a state law or a federal contract, and the people they hire.
items.mechanics: Section 101(6) extends Section 5014 of Division I of P.L. 119-75 for the length of the stopgap.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 101(6)

items.title: Conrad 30 doctor program
items.whatStops: States lose a program that lets doctors trained abroad stay in the U.S. if they work where doctors are scarce.
items.whoFeelsIt: Rural and low-income areas that recruit these doctors, and their patients.
items.mechanics: Section 101(6) extends Section 5013 of Division I of P.L. 119-75, the waiver of the J-1 home residence rule for foreign medical graduates.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 101(6)

items.title: Extra seasonal worker visas (H-2B)
items.whatStops: The authority to add seasonal worker visas above the yearly cap runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: Seasonal employers such as landscapers, resorts and seafood processors.
items.mechanics: Section 101(6) extends Section 5016 of Division I of P.L. 119-75. Section 5015, special immigrant status for religious workers who are not ministers, is extended the same way.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 101(6)

items.title: Livestock price reports
items.whatStops: The law that makes meatpackers report what they pay for cattle, hogs and lambs runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: Ranchers and farmers who use USDA price reports to sell their animals.
items.mechanics: Section 119 extends the Livestock Mandatory Reporting Act of 1999 for the length of the stopgap. It was last fully reauthorized in 2015 (P.L. 114-54).

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 119

items.title: Wildland firefighter pay
items.whatStops: A waiver ends that lets federal wildland firefighters earn extra pay above the normal cap for emergency fire work.
items.whoFeelsIt: Forest Service and Interior Department fire crews.
items.mechanics: Section 142 waives the premium pay cap for emergency wildland fire suppression for the length of the stopgap.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 142

items.title: Federal grant rules rewrite
items.whatStops: A ban ends that keeps the White House budget office from finishing its proposed rewrite of federal grant rules.
items.whoFeelsIt: Cities, counties, schools, universities and nonprofits that get federal grants.
items.mechanics: Section 157 bars issuing or finalizing the May 29, 2026 proposed Uniform Guidance rule (91 FR 32198), or a substantially similar rule, through December 11, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 157

items.title: Commodity fraud whistleblower program
items.whatStops: Authority runs out for the program that pays people who report fraud in commodity and futures markets.
items.whoFeelsIt: People who report market fraud, and investors who rely on those tips.
items.mechanics: Section 134 extends the CFTC whistleblower authority through December 11, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49353, Section 134

items.title: Veterans programs
items.whatStops: Several VA programs run out, including help for homeless veterans, rural veterans and family caregivers.
items.whoFeelsIt: Veterans who are homeless or at risk, rural veterans, and the families who care for veterans.
items.mechanics: Division D, Department of Veterans Affairs Extenders, moves most dates from September 30, 2026 to December 11, 2026. For example, Sec. 4304 provides $130,191,781 for Supportive Services for Veteran Families for October 1 to December 11, 2026.

sources.label: Senate text of the extension divisions (Aug 2, 2026)

items.title: Other authorities ending Dec 11
items.whatStops: A list of smaller authorities also ends, from EPA chemical review fees to a TSA airport screening pilot.
items.whoFeelsIt: Mostly the agencies and industries involved.
list: EPA fees on chemical makers that pay for chemical safety reviews (TSCA), Div. B Sec. 2005
Defense Production Act authorities, Div. B Sec. 2004
Cybersecurity information sharing protections, Div. B Sec. 2011
Patent and Trademark Office fee setting, Div. B Sec. 2015
Food for Peace, Div. B Sec. 2003
Grain inspection standards, Div. B Sec. 2001
U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, Div. B Sec. 2016
TSA paid screening pilot at up to eight airports, Div. A Sec. 138
items.mechanics: Each section replaces an earlier end date with December 11, 2026. Dates are from the Senate-passed text dated August 2, 2026 and CRS R49353.

sources.label: Senate text of the extension divisions (Aug 2, 2026)
CRS R49353

items.title: Community health centers
items.whatStops: The Community Health Center Fund, a main federal funding stream for local health centers, runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: Patients at community health centers, which see people whether or not they have insurance.

reach.label: patients served by HRSA-funded health centers in 2024

items.mechanics: The fund is authorized by Section 10503(b)(1) of the Affordable Care Act (42 U.S.C. 254b-2(b)(1)). Its current end date is December 31, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027
HRSA, 2024 national health center data

items.title: TANF cash help for families
items.whatStops: Federal funding for TANF, the block grant states use for cash help and job programs for low-income families, runs out.
items.whoFeelsIt: Families with children who get cash help, and the state offices that run the program.

reach.label: families received TANF assistance in FY2024

items.extra: The basic block grant is about $16.4 billion a year.
items.mechanics: P.L. 119-75 funds TANF through December 31, 2026. States would get no new federal TANF money for 2027 until Congress extends it.

sources.label: CRS R48413, TANF Block Grant: A Primer (May 4, 2026)

items.title: Medicare doctor pay boost
items.whatStops: A temporary 2.5% raise in what Medicare pays doctors ends with 2026.
items.whoFeelsIt: Doctors who treat Medicare patients, and the seniors and people with disabilities who see them.
items.mechanics: Section 1848(t)(1) of the Social Security Act provides a 2.5% increase for services furnished during calendar year 2026. A floor of 1.0 on the physician work geographic index (Sec. 1848(e)(1)(E)) also ends December 31, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027

items.title: Rural hospital payments
items.whatStops: Two extra Medicare payments for small and rural hospitals end: the low-volume hospital adjustment and the Medicare-dependent hospital program.
items.whoFeelsIt: Small rural hospitals with few patients or many Medicare patients, and the towns that rely on them.
items.mechanics: Social Security Act Sec. 1886(d)(12)(D) (low-volume hospitals) and Sec. 1886(d)(5)(G) (Medicare-dependent hospitals), both ending December 31, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027

items.title: National Health Service Corps
items.whatStops: Funding ends for scholarships and loan repayment for doctors, nurses and dentists who work where care is scarce.
items.whoFeelsIt: Clinicians in the program and patients in areas short on care.
items.mechanics: The National Health Service Corps Fund is authorized by ACA Sec. 10503(b)(2) (42 U.S.C. 254-2(b)(2)) through December 31, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027

items.title: Special diabetes programs
items.whatStops: Funding ends for Type 1 diabetes research and for diabetes programs run by the Indian Health Service and tribes.
items.whoFeelsIt: People with Type 1 diabetes, and American Indian and Alaska Native communities.
items.mechanics: Public Health Service Act Sec. 330B(b)(2) (Type 1) and Sec. 330C(c)(2) (programs for Indians), both through December 31, 2026.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027

items.title: Other health items ending Dec 31
items.whatStops: Several smaller health and family programs also end with the year.
items.whoFeelsIt: Teens, families of children with special needs, labs, and public health programs.
list: Personal Responsibility Education Program for teens, SSA Sec. 513
Sexual Risk Avoidance Education, SSA Sec. 510
Family-to-Family Health Information Centers, SSA Sec. 501(c)(1)(A)
Delay of Medicare lab payment cuts, SSA Sec. 1834A
Advance payment model bonus for doctors (1.88% in 2026), SSA Sec. 1833(z)
Several public health emergency and disaster preparedness authorities, PHSA Secs. 319, 319L, 2811A to 2812
items.mechanics: Each ends December 31, 2026 under the law cited, per CRS Table 1.

sources.label: CRS R49126, Expiring Health Provisions: CY2026 and CY2027
